newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan, Palestinians set up Jerusalem land firm.
newsitem.headline: Jordan, Palestinians set up Jerusalem land firm.

text.p: Jordanian and Palestinian businessmen said on Friday they had set up a multi-million dollar firm to buy and develop Arab property in East Jersualem to protect it from Israeli takeover.
They said shareholders of Jerusalem Development and Investment Company (JEDICO) chose a seven-member board of directors to serve for a two-year tenure at its founding meeting on Thursday.
The board, headed by prominent banker Abdul Majid Shoman, the chairman of Jordan's leading Arab Bank, includes some of the most influential members of the expatriate Palestinian business community.

The idea behind the formation of the offshore holding company, registered in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), is to seek investment opportunities in real estate in East Jerusalem which could block further Israeli takeovers of Arab land from Palestinians.

Prominent Jordanian businessman Munib al-Masri, who was also elected to the board and was a driving force behind the creation of the company, said he expected JEDICO to start operations within a month.
JEDICO has $100 million in authorised capital but Masri hoped this would climb to at least half-a- billion-dollars following a fund raising tour aimed at enlisting new Arab investors.

The company hopes to discourage Arabs in Jerusalem from emigrating because of economic hardships by creating jobs and setting up investment ventures including hotels. It would also renovate existing property.
JEDICO will also provide legal advisory services for Jerusalem's Arab residents to help protect and develop their property against Israeli takeover, its founders said.

Investors say they hope the company will act as a counterweight to U.S. Jewish business groups who have aggressively bankrolled land buying in East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.

U.S. Jewish magnate Irving Moskowitz was last month granted a permit by Jerusalem city council to build in East Jerusalem's Arab Ras al-Amood neighbourhood. The permit was later temporarily suspended to defuse Arab anger.
JEDICO also planned to offer soon in a public subscription the remaining shares still uncovered from its initial $100 million authorised capital. Every share carries a par value of $10.
